title: Encode, Think, Decode: Scaling test-time reasoning with recursive latent thoughts
relevance_reason: Re-runs OLMo-2 1B mid-training with a looped subset of middle layers (encoder / recursive block / decoder) chosen by angular-distance analysis.
one_sentence: Loops 4 reasoning-relevant OLMo-2-1B layers (7-4*k-5, chosen by Kneedle on layer-to-layer angular distance) during a re-run of the 50B-token mid-training, improving reasoning benchmarks with no new parameters or data; adds an ACT router variant.
key_contributions: Interpretability-guided layer selection: Kneedle knee points on mean angular distance between consecutive layers define the encoder (first 7 layers) and decoder (last 5 layers); the 4 middle layers are looped.
Mid-training re-run (same data, hyperparameters, parameter count) with fixed k=2..5 iterations; gains concentrate in math and reading comprehension, with little change on factual knowledge.
At equal FLOPs, selective looping beats looping all layers (0-16*2-0) or Huginn-style middle-12 looping (2-12*2-2); an ACT router allows adaptive per-token depth (max 10).

setup.model_sizes: OLMo-2 1B base (16 layers); configuration 7-4*k-5
setup.train_tokens_or_data: OLMo-2 stage-2 mid-training mixture (5e10 tokens), initialized from stage-1 checkpoint
setup.loops_train: fixed k in {2,3,4,5}, one model per k; adaptive ACT variant with Nmax=10
setup.loops_test: same k as training; adaptive variant per-token
setup.baselines: OLMo-2 1B mid-trained identically without recursion (k=1); alternative recursive configs 2-12*2-2 and 0-16*2-0 at matched FLOPs
setup.benchmarks: 17 tasks: TriviaQA, NQ, BoolQ, OpenBookQA, DROP, CSQA, HellaSwag, SocialIQA, WinoGrande, ARC-E/C, MMLU, MMLU-Pro, AGIEval, BBH, GSM8K, MATH

claims.claim: Looping the selected middle layers during mid-training improves the identically mid-trained non-recursive OLMo-2 1B, most on math and reading comprehension; iteration count and FLOPs grow with k (not FLOP-matched to a deeper dense model).
claims.evidence_quote: ETD models yield substantial gains on 17 reasoning benchmarks, including +28.4% relative accuracy improvement on GSM8K and +36% on MATH with the OLMo-2 1B Base model.

claims.claim: Which layers to loop matters: at equal FLOPs, looping the 4 knee-selected layers beats looping all layers or the middle 12 layers.
claims.evidence_quote: Our approach consistently outperforms these alternatives under equal compute. For example, the 2–12*2–2 setup is FLOP-equivalent to our 7–4*4–5 configuration, yet yields lower accuracy.

claims.claim: The best block position depends on task category: 7-4*2-5 is best for math, while an earlier block (3-4*2-9) is best for reading comprehension.
claims.evidence_quote: Interestingly, for reading comprehension, the 3-4*2-9 configuration performs best.

claims.claim: An ACT-style router trained end-to-end gives adaptive depth that tracks the fixed-depth accuracy-iteration trade-off and beats fixed k=5 on DROP and OpenBookQA with fewer average iterations.
claims.evidence_quote: we see that adaptive-depth ETD outperforms the ETD with fixed k=5 iterations. Moreover, it also achieves this with fewer iterations on average.

numbers.what: mid-training share of total tokens
numbers.quote: We evaluate the ETD approach by integrating it into the mid-training stage which uses only 1.25% of the total pretraining tokens.

numbers.what: GSM8K accuracy for OLMo-2 1B (k=1) and ETD k=2,3,4 (Table 3), then relative gains k=2..5 and MATH k=1,2
GSM8K at k=5
math reasoning category relative gain at k=2
numbers.quote: The largest improvement is observed on Mathematical Reasoning tasks, with an average relative increase of 16.3%.

numbers.what: selected configuration
numbers.value: 7 encoder layers, 4 recursive layers, 5 decoder layers
numbers.quote: Hence, we set the configuration to 7-4*k-5, i,e. 7 layers in latent encoder, 4 layer in recursive block, and 5 layers in latent decoder respectively

numbers.what: ACT halting threshold and cap
numbers.quote: Computation for a token is stopped once Ht ≥ 1 − ϵ, with ϵ is a small constant (e.g. 0.01), and the maximum possible number of iterations is Nmax =10.

numbers.what: MATH accuracy and relative change at k=2,3,4,5 (Table 3; base 4.57)

limitations: Only OLMo-2 1B base; one data order per configuration; each k trained separately; no FLOP-matched deeper dense baseline; MATH gains are on a very low base (4.57%) and reverse at k=4-5; instruct/post-training integration left to future work.
builds_on: Gromov et al. 2024 (layer pruning, angular distance)
survey_notes: Key (d) evidence on which layers to loop. Caveat for the survey: the headline +36% MATH is relative on a 4.57% base (5.45 at k=2, 6.22 at k=3) and MATH falls below baseline at k=4 (3.73) and k=5 (4.33), so the MATH claim is fragile; GSM8K gains are monotone (44.05 to 56.56). Regime: iso-param + iso-data vs the same OLMo-2 mid-training; the looped model uses more inference FLOPs and there is no deeper dense baseline. Agrees with 2511.07384 that looping middle/late layers with fixed prelude/coda works, but disagrees on details: ETD keeps all layers, uses no input injection, fixed k; 2511.07384 drops middle layers, loops later layers, and uses Huginn's concat adapter with a random initial state. ETD's layer-choice criterion (angular-distance knee) contrasts with 2511.07384's small search and 2610.00673's whole-stack looping.

title: Bridging the Gap Between Latent and Explicit Reasoning with Looped Transformers
relevance_reason: Fine-tunes pretrained Llama/GPT-2 models into looped padded Transformers (whole model iterated R times over latent blocks) with parallel CoT-token supervision.
one_sentence: LOTUS turns a CoT-finetuned LM into a looped padded Transformer: K=6 latent blocks refined in parallel for R=6 full-model iterations, supervised post-loop against gold CoT tokens through the LM head; matches explicit CoT on GSM8K at 3B with 2.5x faster thinking.
key_contributions: Post-training recipe: learnable padded latent blocks, input-injected loop of the whole pretrained LM with gradients through all R iterations, cross-entropy of post-loop latents against gold CoT-step tokens plus answer loss (lambda_step=0.05), with a Coconut-style curriculum that grows latent blocks and loops together.

At Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, GSM8K within about 1.5 points of explicit CoT and better out-of-domain average, where prior latent-CoT methods trail by up to 9.2 points; thought-phase latency 2.5x (math expressions) to 6.9x (natural language) lower.

Ablations: post-loop readout beats per-iteration readout for direct LM-head supervision; accuracy rises steeply with trained loop depth R (14.6% at R=2 to 70.0% at R=6) and running more loops than trained does not help.

setup.train_tokens_or_data: GSM8k-Aug (385k samples); natural-language GSM8K-Aug for the stress test; 30 epochs
setup.loops_train: R=6 (curriculum R_e = K_e grows with converted CoT steps); ablation R=2..6
setup.loops_test: R=6; inference sweep R=1..7
setup.baselines: Explicit CoT and No-CoT on same backbone and data; CODI, CODI+SIM-CoT, Coconut, PCCoT, KaVa
setup.benchmarks: GSM8K (in-domain), GSM-Hard, MultiArith, SVAMP

claims.claim: At 3B, the looped padded model with parallel gold-CoT supervision brings latent reasoning to within about 1 point of explicit CoT on GSM8K (same backbone, same data), unlike prior latent methods whose gap widens with scale.
claims.regime: iso_param + iso_data (explicit CoT uses more sequential decoding)
claims.evidence_quote: on L LAMA -3.2-3B-I NSTRUCT, it brings the GSM8K test accuracy to within 1 point of explicit CoT and surpasses explicit CoT on the out-ofdomain math average.

claims.claim: For direct LM-head supervision, reading only the post-loop latents beats supervising every iteration; the auxiliary-decoder variant prefers per-iteration readout.
claims.evidence_quote: LOTUS performs best with post-loop readout (70.0% vs. 68.2% per-iter), which lets the early latent blocks refine fully until the end of the loop.

claims.claim: Trained loop depth matters strongly and extra test-time loops beyond the trained depth do not help.
claims.evidence_quote: Accuracy climbs with R (22.7% at R“1 to 70.0% at R“6), peaks at the trained R“6, and dips slightly at R“7 (69.3%).

claims.claim: The looped padded backbone helps even without latent supervision, and gold-CoT supervision adds further gains.
claims.evidence_quote: Without any latent supervision, the looped backbone alone (63.3%) already exceeds CODI + SIM-CoT (62.3%, Table 1), which uses a single latent per step

numbers.value: CODI + SIM-CoT trails explicit CoT by 9.2 points
numbers.quote: CODI + SIM-CoT is level with explicit CoT at GPT-2 (42.6 vs. 42.7) yet trails it by 9.2 points at 3B

numbers.value: 68.13 vs 68.41 accuracy; 140.8 vs 963.6 ms thought latency (6.9x)
numbers.quote: LOTUS is on par with explicit CoT in accuracy (68.13 vs. 68.41) while cutting thought-phase latency from 963.6 ms to 140.8 ms with a 6.9ˆ speedup.

numbers.quote: accuracy rises steeply with R (from 14.6% at R“2 to 70.0% at R“6), with gains continuing through R“5 (68.1%) before nearly saturating at R“6.

numbers.value: 133.0 ms LOTUS vs 338.8 ms explicit CoT

survey_notes: Belongs in (e) post-training/SFT into a looped model and (c) supervision design. Loops the entire pretrained LM over a padded latent workspace (looping is over depth, applied to latent positions only, with the question prefix KV-cached once). Full BPTT through R=6 iterations of a 3B model. Supervision finding (post-loop readout beats per-iteration readout for the LM-head route) is a counterpoint to per-loop/deep-supervision objectives used by Ouro-style training (2510.25741, 2610.00673); 2606.24898 in this group studies readout too. Uses a curriculum that grows loops with latent blocks (Coconut-style). Regime: vs explicit CoT on the same backbone and data (iso_param, iso_data); inference compute is not matched (LOTUS is cheaper in latency). No extrapolation beyond trained R, consistent with many fixed-R looped models.

title: Architectural Sampling: Test-Time Scaling via Computational Diversity in Frozen Vision Language Models
relevance_reason: Training-free repetition of a contiguous decoder-layer window in frozen VLMs, used to diversify sampled candidates rather than to deepen a single answer.
one_sentence: Builds a pool of candidates from a frozen Qwen VLM by repeating different contiguous decoder-layer windows r times (each window/r pair is one computation path); pass@9 rises 6.58 points over temperature sampling, best with early-layer windows.
key_contributions: Training-free candidate generation from distinct computation paths (window location x repetition count) with no weight updates or added parameters.
Early-layer windows give the largest gains; jointly reprocessing visual and language tokens is best; gains hold under greedy decoding.
Architectural rollouts replace temperature rollouts in label-free GRPO test-time RL (TTRV) and improve pass@1.

setup.model_sizes: Qwen2.5-VL-7B, Qwen3-VL-2B/8B, Qwen3.5-VL-2B/4B
setup.train_tokens_or_data: none (training-free); TTRV uses 20 unlabeled samples with LoRA
setup.loops_test: window repeated r times, up to depth 4 in the cost analysis
setup.baselines: temperature sampling, beam search, top-k, top-p from the same frozen model at equal candidate count
setup.benchmarks: 12 multimodal benchmarks incl. AI2D, ScienceQA, CV-Bench, MMStar, BLINK, A-OKVQA

claims.claim: At equal candidate count (9), candidates from repeated-layer paths cover more correct answers than temperature samples of the standard path; per-candidate compute is higher, so not FLOP-matched.
claims.regime: iso_param (same frozen checkpoint), equal candidate count, not iso_infer_flop
claims.evidence_quote: Across five Qwen checkpoints and twelve multimodal benchmarks, architectural sampling improves pass@9 over standardpath temperature sampling by 6.58 percentage points on average at the same ninecandidate budget.

claims.claim: Which layers to repeat: early windows give the highest pass@9; gains fall as the window moves deeper.
claims.evidence_quote: Every region improves over temperature sampling, but the gain falls as the window moves deeper. Reusing the early layers gives the highest pass@9 on all five benchmarks

numbers.what: largest and smallest checkpoint-level pass@9 gains
numbers.quote: The largest checkpoint-level gains are observed for Qwen3VL-8B (+12.43 points) and Qwen3.5-VL-4B (+9.13 points), while the smallest gain is +1.10 points for Qwen3.5-VL-2B.

numbers.what: latency overhead of recursion
numbers.value: roughly 1-2 s more, up to depth 4
numbers.quote: the overhead is marginal (roughly 1–2 seconds more, depending on recursion depth, up to depth 4)

limitations: Higher per-candidate forward cost than temperature sampling; requires access to internal layers (not usable for API-only models).
builds_on: 2507.07996 (CoLa, Skip a Layer or Loop it)
survey_notes: (d) training-free looping: here layer repetition is used as a diversity source for best-of-n and test-time RL, not as a single-answer improvement; claims are pass@k at equal candidate count, not FLOP-matched. Its finding that early-layer windows work best contrasts with retrofit papers that loop middle/late layers (2510.07358 ETD loops the middle block; 2511.07384 loops later layers) and should be noted as task/objective-dependent (diversity vs accuracy).

title: Don't Commit Alone: Joint Token Commitment in Diffusion Language Models
relevance_reason: Re-applies the last n layers of a diffusion LM once (a single partial extra pass) to coordinate jointly committed tokens; layer reuse, not iterated recurrence.
one_sentence: For LLaDA2.1-mini, a marker vector flags the tokens to be committed and the backbone's last n=3 layers are re-applied once to coordinate them before writing; with LoRA and markers trained on 50k FineWeb-Edu documents, 5 of 7 benchmarks improve.
key_contributions: Frames parallel-commit error as conditional total correlation and adds a marker-gated coordination pass that reuses the last n layers.
Re-applying layers without the marker reduces accuracy; deeper coordination (n=6, 9) gives no consistent gain over n=3.

setup.model_sizes: LLaDA2.1-mini (frozen backbone + LoRA + marker vectors)
setup.train_tokens_or_data: 50k FineWeb-Edu documents
setup.loops_train: one extra pass over last n=3 layers (ablation n=6, 9)
setup.loops_test: K=1 coordination round
setup.baselines: released LLaDA2.1-mini factorized decoder; same weights with Stage B disabled
setup.benchmarks: GSM8K, CMATH, DROP, PIQA, GPQA, HumanEval+, MBPP+

claims.claim: Extra layer reuse helps only with the marker signal: re-applying the last n layers without the marker lowers GSM8K accuracy, so the gain is not just added depth.
claims.evidence_quote: Re-applying the last n layers without a marker reduces accuracy by 0.76 points, indicating that the marker announcement contributes beyond additional depth.

claims.claim: Re-applying more layers does not help: n=3 beats n=6 and n=9 on average.
claims.evidence_quote: Averaged over the seven benchmarks, n=3 scores 78.72, compared with 77.50 for n=6 and 77.65 for n=9.

numbers.what: per-benchmark gains over released decoder
numbers.quote: Table 1 shows that C O C OMMIT improves code generation (HumanEval+ +5.49, MBPP+ +1.33), physical commonsense (PIQA +3.70), graduate-level science QA (GPQA +3.03), and grade-school math (GSM8K +1.52).

numbers.what: decomposition of gain on GSM8K
numbers.quote: With Stage B disabled, our weights improve by 1.14 points over the released model, capturing the effect of the adapters and CPT data. Enabling Stage B at the same weights adds another 0.38 points.

limitations: Single dLLM checkpoint; most of the GSM8K gain comes from adapter training rather than the coordination pass; deeper reuse not beneficial.
survey_notes: Peripheral to (d): shows one extra pass over the last layers can be trained cheaply with LoRA, but the decomposition attributes only +0.38 of the GSM8K gain to the extra pass, and raw layer re-application without the learned marker hurts. Not a recurrent-depth model; cite at most in a footnote on layer reuse in diffusion LMs.

title: Port-Hamiltonian Latent Deliberation: Mitigating the Deliberation Drift Cliff in Test-Time Compute Scaling
relevance_reason: Constrains an iterated continuous latent 'thought' vector with dissipative Hamiltonian/Helmholtz-Hodge flows to stop drift beyond the trained horizon; toy-scale, not a looped transformer LM.
one_sentence: Shows unconstrained recurrent latent deliberation collapses when iterated far beyond training horizons (drift cliff) and proposes dissipative geometric flows (DG-HHD) that keep accuracy at deep steps, on synthetic graphs and a tiny ProofWriter model.
key_contributions: Names the 'deliberation drift cliff': gains at K<=4 collapse at K>=16 for unconstrained recurrent latent models.
Trade-off: strictly conservative (curl-free) flows suppress drift but cap accuracy; DG-HHD decouples a dissipative potential part from circulation.

setup.model_sizes: compact deliberation models, Dmodel 128-256
setup.train_tokens_or_data: synthetic relational multi-hop graphs; ProofWriter
setup.loops_test: K up to 64
setup.baselines: unconstrained recurrent baselines, conservative HHD, autoregressive baseline
setup.benchmarks: synthetic multi-hop graphs; ProofWriter

claims.claim: Unconstrained recurrent latent updates diverge out of distribution when iterated well past the training horizon; dissipative constraints prevent this.
claims.evidence_quote: an unconstrained baseline (B0-Naive) suffers a catastrophic drop from a peak of 96.60% at K = 4 down to 34.13% at K = 64 (∆ = −62.47%).

numbers.what: conservative vs unconstrained flows trade-off
numbers.value: conservative: 3.40% cliff, 32.73% peak; unconstrained: 82.33% peak, 36.87% cliff
numbers.quote: completely suppressing long-range drift (cliff 3.40%) but bottlenecking peak reasoning accuracy at 32.73% ± 1.10%

limitations: Compact models (Dmodel 128-256) on synthetic deduction tasks; single continuous thought vector, not token-sequence recurrence; scaling to LLMs left open. Survey caution: unconventional reporting (e.g. '22-round investigation', 'certified invariants') and large seed variance (+-13.61, +-14.93).
survey_notes: (b) stability: supports the general finding that unconstrained recurrence drifts beyond the trained horizon and contractive/dissipative structure fixes it at some cost in expressivity (cf. STARS 2605.26733 spectral-radius penalty, 2607.10681 spectral margin). Toy-scale with high variance; cite only as weak corroboration.

key_contributions: Early-layer attention duplication (1-2 copies) as a training-free or fine-tuned enhancement (abstract only).

claims.evidence_quote: The re-sults demonstrate that duplicating the initial layers once or twice often yields a significant performance boost.

title: MACRO: Markov Chain Routing of Transformer Layers
relevance_reason: Training-free task-level layer routing (skip, repeat, residual add) over frozen pretrained LLMs; repeats layers but is not a trained weight-tied recurrent model.
one_sentence: Learns one task-level Markov policy over skip/repeat/add-hidden-state layer moves on a frozen LLM via cross-entropy-method search on ~1000 training examples, decodes top-k routes with Viterbi, and improves accuracy over the unrouted model and Dr.LLM.
key_contributions: Layer routing as a context-dependent Markov policy (layer, budget phase, displacement, op context) searched without gradients or weight updates.
Exact top-k Viterbi decoding plus validation selection replaces per-example search and router training.
Gains are largest on weak/small models; routes partly transfer across related math tasks.

setup.model_sizes: Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-14B (4-bit), Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct (4-bit), DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B; Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct in appendix

setup.loops_train: Routes capped at 40-52 block calls (e.g. 40 for Qwen3-1.7B with 28 layers); local move radius r=5
setup.loops_test: One fixed searched route per task (e.g. 33 block calls on Qwen3-1.7B GSM8K route)
setup.baselines: Unrouted forward pass, Dr.LLM, Dr.LLM with MACRO action space
setup.benchmarks: GSM8K, MATH500, MedQA, OpenBookQA, SciQ, MMLU-Pro, SVAMP, ASDiv, MAWPS, GSM8K-Hard, GSM8K-Plus, multistep arithmetic, object counting

claims.claim: Task-level routing of a frozen LLM improves average accuracy over the unrouted model and over Dr.LLM while cutting route-search time.
claims.regime: iso_param vs unrouted same model; inference FLOPs not matched (routes can be longer than the standard pass)
claims.evidence_quote: MACRO achieves a +5.0% average accuracy improvement over the unrouted baselines, with largest gains on small models. We outperform the best dynamic routing approach Dr. LLM by +7.2%, while reducing route-search time 9.4× (from 14.8 to 1.6 hours).

claims.claim: Gains shrink as the base model gets stronger: large on Qwen3-1.7B and the R1-distilled model, under 1 point on Qwen3-8B/14B.
claims.evidence_quote: its margin over the unrouted baseline is widest exactly where that baseline is weakest, narrowing to a smaller but consistent gain once the model is already strong

claims.claim: The action space (including residual addition of earlier hidden states) matters more than the router: Dr.LLM's skip-and-repeat space often falls below baseline, while the same routers with MACRO's action space are much stronger.
claims.evidence_quote: indicating that the action space itself is a decisive part of what makes layer routing help rather than hurt

claims.claim: Logit-lens analysis suggests routing exposes an answer already computed internally rather than adding new reasoning.
claims.evidence_quote: this suggests that routing improves how an already-computed answer is exposed rather than changing the reasoning itself

numbers.quote: rewinding Qwen3-1.7B from layer 7 back to layer 3 and replaying five blocks raises test accuracy from 43.4% to 69.5%, without changing a single weight

numbers.quote: yielding a +5.0% average accuracy improvement over the nonrouted baseline, +7.2% over Dr. LLM, and +1.5% over Dr. LLM with an equivalent action space, while reducing the route-search computational cost by 9.4×

Search budget

numbers.quote: The main experiments use 10 search iterations with 30 candidate programs per iteration.

numbers.what: Inference cost of a revisited block
numbers.value: T applied steps cost as a T-block tied-weight network
numbers.quote: a route of T applied steps has the cache and decoding cost of a T -block network with tied weights

limitations: Routes are task-level (not input-dependent) and need labeled training/validation examples; per-token compute and KV cache grow with route length; the authors argue gains may come from eliciting an internally present answer rather than new capability; no gain on the reasoning-distilled model versus Dr.LLM+Ext.
survey_notes: Section (d) training-free looping: frozen Qwen3 gains from replaying a contiguous mid-stack block (L3-L7 of 28) agree with ETD/ inner-loop papers that a middle block is the right segment to loop. Comparison is iso-param but not iso-inference-FLOP; gains are task-specific and need labeled data for search, and vanish on strong models (<1 pt on 8B/14B), so 'training-free looping helps' is a weak-model, task-tuned result. The residual 'add earlier hidden state' action resembles input/history injection in trained looped models (Huginn) and is what makes Dr.LLM's routers useful in this paper.

title: Skip a Layer or Loop It? Learning Program-of-Layers in LLMs
relevance_reason: Training-free looping/skipping of contiguous segments of frozen pretrained LLMs, with a learned 2.1M-parameter program predictor; direct evidence on which layers to loop in pretrained models.
one_sentence: MCTS over skip/repeat programs of frozen LLM layers shows better programs exist for most inputs (oracle), then a small predictor trained on MCTS traces outputs per-input segment skip/keep/repeat programs that beat standard inference and dynamic-depth baselines on math.
key_contributions: Oracle MCTS study: joint skip+loop programs beat skip-only or loop-only; valid programs are mostly short contiguous segments repeated at most once.

PoLar predictor (frozen Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B encoder + layer-query cross-attention, ~2.1M params) predicts segment boundaries and skip/keep/repeat labels per input, supervised by MCTS-found valid programs.
Gains at pass@1 and pass@k over sampling, with lower latency on average and OOD transfer to ASDiv, MAWPS, MMLU-Pro.

setup.model_sizes: LLaMA-3.2-3B-Instruct, Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat, Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, Qwen3-8B (all frozen)
setup.train_tokens_or_data: Predictor trained on MCTS-derived valid programs for DART-Math: 4,130 training, 826 validation, 1,651 test examples
setup.loops_train: Segments of at most Kmax=4 contiguous layers; repeat = one extra pass of a segment
setup.loops_test: Per-input predicted program; top-k beam candidates for pass@k

title: Programs-of-Layers in LLMs through the Lens of Cortical Areas

Finds error-correcting programs are fragile and MMLU-Pro rescuing programs overfit to answer position.

title: Skip a Layer or Loop it? Test-Time Depth Adaptation of Pretrained LLMs
relevance_reason: Per-sample test-time search over skipping and repeating layers of frozen pretrained LLMs (training-free looping of pretrained layers).
one_sentence: Uses per-input MCTS with gold-answer reward to find chains of skipped/repeated layers of frozen LLaMA-3 and OLMoE models, showing large oracle accuracy gains and that most inputs admit shorter layer paths.
key_contributions: Defines chain-of-layers (CoLa): per-sample paths that skip or repeat contiguous blocks (k, r in 1..4) of a frozen pretrained model.
MCTS (200 simulations per input, length penalty) with correctness reward finds better or shorter paths for most samples.
Layer-usage analysis: early layers are always kept, middle layers are most often skipped in small models; larger and instruction-tuned models use layers more uniformly.

setup.model_sizes: LLaMA-3-3B, LLaMA-3-8B, OLMoE-1B-7B, base and instruction-tuned variants (frozen)
setup.train_tokens_or_data: No training; 500 sampled instances per dataset; MCTS feedback from gold answers
setup.loops_test: Repeat a block of k layers r times, k, r in {1,2,3,4}; path length constrained
setup.baselines: Original forward pass; skip-only and recurrence-only search spaces
setup.benchmarks: ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, DART-Math levels 1-5

claims.claim: With per-sample oracle search, shorter paths exist for most correctly answered samples and correcting paths exist for most wrongly answered samples.
claims.regime: iso_param; oracle (MCTS uses gold-answer correctness on the evaluated input), so an upper bound
claims.evidence_quote: For >75% of samples with correct predictions by the original LLM, we can find shorter CoLa, suggesting a large space for improving inference efficiency; (2) For >60% of samples with originally incorrect predictions, we can identify CoLa achieving correct predictions

claims.claim: Joint skip+recurrence search beats skip-only and recurrence-only on all datasets and models; skip-only is stronger on easy ARC tasks, recurrence-only on harder DART levels for instruct models.
claims.evidence_quote: Our full method, which searches over both skipping and recurrence decisions, consistently achieves the highest accuracy on all datasets and models.

claims.claim: Recurrence-only gains come with increased depth; error-correcting paths are often shorter than the full model, suggesting 'overthinking' in depth.
claims.evidence_quote: Recurrence-only strategies achieve moderate gains over the pretrained baseline, but do so by increasing the overall depth

claims.claim: Early layers are kept; skipping concentrates in middle layers, most sharply in small pretrained models.
claims.evidence_quote: CoLa models consistently keep early layers but exhibit an elevated skip rate of middle layers.

numbers.what: LLaMA-3-3B base ARC-E accuracy, original vs skip-only (oracle)
numbers.quote: For example, on LLaMA-3B, accuracy on ARC-E improves from 27.8% to 75.4%, showing that reducing computation depth can be beneficial

numbers.what: LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct DART-2: skip-only, recurrence-only, full CoLa (oracle)
numbers.quote: on DART-2, the LLaMA-3-8B-Instr model improves from 25.2% (skip-only) and 22.0% (recurrence-only) to 66.2% with the full space

numbers.what: MCTS budget and length penalty
numbers.quote: We use 200 simulations per input in our MCTS implementation for optimizing CoLa, balancing search quality and runtime.

numbers.what: LLaMA-3-3B base, original / skip-only / recurrence-only / CoLa (oracle): ARC-E then ARC-C
numbers.quote: Original +Skip-only +Recurrence-only +CoLa (Skip+Recurrence) 27.80 75.40 65.40 95.80 20.80 75.60 54.80 98.20

survey_notes: Section (d): precursor to PoLar (2606.06574) and MACRO (2608.05872). All headline gains are per-sample oracle search with test labels, so they measure the existence of better paths, not a method. Contradiction: CoLa Table 1 often has skip-only > recurrence-only (e.g. ARC and base-model DART), whereas PoLar Finding 1 and RE-PoLar (2609.31360) report recurrence-only > skip-only on DART-Math; CoLa's text also says DART-2 recurrence-only is 22.0% while its Table 1 lists 20.80. Baseline accuracies of base models are near floor (zero-shot formatting), so oracle path search partly fixes output formatting.

title: Inner Loop Inference for Pretrained Transformers: Unlocking Latent Capabilities Without Training
relevance_reason: Training-free middle-block looping of frozen pretrained LLMs (Gemma 2, Llama 3) with hidden-state interpolation to stabilize repeated application.
one_sentence: Re-applies a selected middle block of frozen Gemma 2 and Llama 3 models at inference; naive looping always hurts, while interpolating looped states with cached/baseline states gives small gains on Gemma and inconsistent results on pre-norm Llama.
key_contributions: Middle-looping of a frozen model (prelude once, block s..e-1 repeated R times, coda once) with representation interpolation (uniform average, moving average to baseline, auto-alignment softmax) to limit distribution shift.
Shows naive looping of a pretrained block degrades accuracy for every start-end configuration on Gemma2-2B WinoGrande.
Best loop region sits at roughly 40-60% relative depth; matched-magnitude noise control underperforms structured looping.

setup.model_sizes: Gemma 2 2B and 9B, Llama 3 8B (frozen)
setup.train_tokens_or_data: No training; loop region selected by sweeping on WinoGrande
setup.loops_test: Naive sweep uses loop count 3; one model-specific loop region (e.g. Gemma 2-2B layers 10-13) fixed across tasks
setup.baselines: Same frozen model without looping; matched-magnitude noise injection
setup.benchmarks: WinoGrande, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, GSM8K, HellaSwag, MMLU (lighteval)

claims.claim: Naively repeating a block of a frozen pretrained model degrades accuracy for every tested start-end configuration, some collapsing toward chance, consistent with distribution shift of activations.
claims.regime: iso_param (same frozen model, more inference FLOPs)
claims.evidence_quote: All looped configurations perform worse than the baseline accuracy, with some settings collapsing to near-chance performance.

claims.claim: Interpolating looped states (uniform averaging of cached loop states) yields modest gains on Gemma models; Llama-3-8B (pure pre-norm) responds inconsistently.
claims.evidence_quote: this yields modest but consistent accuracy gains for Gemma models, while Llama 3–8B responds less reliably, due to architectural differences.

claims.claim: The best loop region is in the middle of the network (about 40-60% depth).
claims.evidence_quote: the selected intervals consistently fall within comparable relative depths, roughly 40–60% of the network, matching the stage-wise inference dynamics reported in [2].

claims.claim: Normalization placement matters for stability of repeated application: pre-norm is described as less stable under repetition than Gemma 2's pre+post norm.
claims.evidence_quote: most modern LLMs rely on pre-layer normalization, which improves optimization during training but is known to be less stable when blocks are repeatedly applied

numbers.what: Gemma 2-2B WinoGrande (5-shot): baseline vs Uniform interpolation
Gemma 2-2B GSM8K (5-shot): baseline, Uniform, Moving Average, Auto-Align, Noise
Llama 3-8B MMLU (5-shot): baseline vs Uniform (looping hurts)
Best loop region for Gemma 2-2B
numbers.quote: In the case of Gemma 2-2B, the best configuration corresponds to looping layers 10–13 (see Figure 1).

limitations: Gains are small and mostly within the reported standard errors; loop region tuned on WinoGrande; Llama 3-8B gains are unreliable; only three models up to 9B; no wall-clock or FLOP accounting.
builds_on: Saunshi et al. Reasoning with latent thoughts
survey_notes: Section (d) and (b): direct evidence that naive training-free looping of a pretrained block is harmful (distribution shift), which agrees with retrofit papers that require continued training (2511.07384, ETD 2510.07358) and with RE-PoLar/PoLar that at most one repeat of short segments helps. The fix here is a training-free analogue of stabilizing state passing (averaging/interpolating with the non-looped state, akin to damping or residual scaling). Effect sizes (<1 point mostly, within ±1-3.6 std errors) are much smaller than MACRO/PoLar task-tuned gains; the middle-depth loop region (40-60%) agrees with RE-PoLar's best repeat block (layers 18-22 of 36 on Qwen3-8B, 2609.31360), while MACRO's example GSM8K route replays earlier layers (L3-L7 of 28, 2608.05872).

title: Training-Free Looped Transformers
relevance_reason: Loops a contiguous mid-stack window of frozen pretrained LLMs at inference with no training.
one_sentence: Inference-time wrapper re-applies a mid-depth window of a frozen checkpoint as damped Euler / Runge-Kutta sub-steps rather than naive repetition; naive looping degrades, damped sub-stepping gives small gains (about +1 to +2.6 pp) on knowledge MC benchmarks across 7 families.
key_contributions: Views each pre-norm block as a forward Euler step at h=1; replaces naive K-fold looping with K damped sub-steps (h=1/K) that target the same endpoint the post-loop layers were trained on.
Block-mode vs layer-mode iteration; layer-mode needed on MoE checkpoints to avoid expert-routing thrash.
Depth-fraction rule for which layers to loop (window center at about 0.45-0.60 of depth) across dense and MoE models from 16 to 48 layers.

setup.model_sizes: Qwen3 0.6B/1.7B/4B (base and instruct), Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct, Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat, Llama-3.2 1B/3B-Instruct, DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, Moonlight-16B-A3B-Instruct
setup.train_tokens_or_data: none (frozen checkpoints)
setup.loops_test: K in {1..24} in ablations; out-of-the-box recipe uses K-stage Runge-Kutta on the mid 4 layers (K=2-3)
setup.baselines: same frozen checkpoint without looping; naive K-fold looping; uniform loop of Inner Loop Inference (2602.14759); Anderson, heavy-ball, Aitken, higher-order RK solvers
setup.benchmarks: lm-eval-harness knowledge MC (MMLU-Pro, GPQA-Main, MMLU, ARC-Challenge, CommonsenseQA, OpenBookQA) plus a 16-task macro suite

claims.claim: Naive K-fold reapplication of a mid block in a frozen model degrades accuracy almost universally, because post-loop layers were trained on the one-pass endpoint.
claims.regime: iso_param (same frozen checkpoint, extra inference compute)
claims.evidence_quote: But the post-loop layers are not trained to receive the trajectory at t=K, and empirically, naive K-fold looping degrades performance almost universally (Section 3).

claims.claim: Damped sub-stepping (K Euler steps of size 1/K, or K-stage RK with anchor) keeps iterates in the trained regime and improves over the unlooped checkpoint on most cells.
claims.evidence_quote: The principled goal of g (K) is therefore not to advance integration to t=K, but to better approximate the same endpoint x(t=1) that the unmodified network already targets.

claims.claim: Which layers to loop: the optimal window sits at a stable fractional depth across architectures; MoE models need layer-mode iteration.
claims.evidence_quote: A universal depth-fraction rule places the optimal window at fractional depth ≈0.45–0.60 across dense and MoE architectures from 16 to 48 layers.

claims.claim: Higher-order solvers and fixed-point accelerators do not beat simple damped sub-stepping, suggesting the looped middle of a pretrained transformer is not contractive.
claims.evidence_quote: find none robustly beats K-stage Runge–Kutta, suggesting the looped middle of a pretrained transformer [35, 77, 5] is not contractive in any useful sense

numbers.what: Headline gains over the unlooped frozen checkpoint
numbers.quote: our method improves Qwen3-4B-Instruct by +2.64 pp on MMLU-Pro, Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct by +1.14 pp on CommonsenseQA

numbers.what: Share of (model, benchmark) cells non-negative under the fixed recipe
numbers.quote: 87% of cells across seven model families and our benchmark suite are non-negative under the fixed out-of-the-box recipe with no per-cell hyperparameter tuning.

numbers.what: Cell breakdown: positive vs neutral
numbers.quote: resulting in 27 positive (∆ > +0.3 pp, 60%) and 12 neutral (|∆| ≤ 0.3 pp, 27%) cells.

numbers.what: Naive looping collapse on 16-task macro (Qwen3-1.7B-Base)
numbers.quote: The naive loop variant degrades monotonically, falling to 37.89% at K=6 (-17.71 pp).

numbers.what: Toy model MSE: naive K=8 looping vs damped sub-step
numbers.quote: at K=8 this degrades to a MSE of 335 versus the sub-step value of 1.04 (≈ 320× gap).

numbers.what: Compute used for experiments
numbers.quote: Approximately 20,000 NVIDIA H100 HBM3-80GB GPU hours were used for the experiments.

limitations: Gains are small (roughly +1 to +2.6 pp) and concentrated on knowledge-heavy multiple-choice benchmarks; negatives concentrate in sub-3B distilled checkpoints; MLA-based MoE models show 3-4x smaller gains; Table 3 reports the best loop configuration per model family, so headline cells involve configuration selection (Table 4 is the leakage-free check).
survey_notes: Training-free retrofit (sub-theme d). Key message for the survey: post-loop layers expect the one-pass endpoint, so naive repetition fails and looping must be damped (convex mix x <- (1-1/K)x + (1/K)g(x)); this is the inference-time analogue of residual scaling / damping fixes used in trained loops. Directly contradicts the simple uniform repetition of 2602.14759, which they report fails to scale after K>=6. Depth-fraction rule (middle layers ~0.45-0.60) agrees with ETD (2510.07358) and other papers that loop middle 'reasoning' layers. Regime is iso_param with more inference FLOPs, not iso_infer_flop. Gains are modest and selection-sensitive.

title: Entropy-Gated Latent Recursion
relevance_reason: Training-free re-application of a frozen LLM's top-L decoder layers at high-entropy tokens, used as a deterministic sampling axis.
one_sentence: At high-entropy tokens a frozen LLM re-applies its top-L layers to an anchor-fused, norm-matched state until the next-token distribution converges; varying L gives deterministic rollout diversity that, aggregated by majority vote, beats greedy and FLOP-matched beam search on math.
key_contributions: Training-free top-L layer recursion gated by token entropy (about 5% of tokens trigger) with KL-based early exit and Kmax=3.
Stabilization of training-free recursion by fusing the refined state with the layer N-L anchor (small alpha) and norm-matching; large alpha collapses accuracy.
Layer span L as a deterministic sampling axis complementary to temperature; EGLR-SC majority vote over L.

setup.model_sizes: 8 frozen instruction-tuned models 0.5B-14B (Qwen2.5-0.5B/3B/7B/14B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B/7B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3)
setup.train_tokens_or_data: none (frozen)
setup.loops_test: Kmax=3 iterations of top-L layers, L in {1..10}, KL early exit
setup.baselines: greedy decoding of same model, self-consistency at matched samples, beam search B=4 and B=11 (FLOP-matched to full L sweep)
setup.benchmarks: GSM8K, MATH-500, MinervaMath, AMC23, AIME24, AIME25

claims.claim: Majority vote over the L-axis rollout pool improves over greedy decoding of the same frozen model on almost all cells, and beats FLOP-matched beam search.
claims.regime: iso_param vs greedy (about 11x more compute); iso_infer_flop vs Beam-11
claims.evidence_quote: EGLR-SC improves over greedy on 44/48 (model, dataset) cells across 8 instruction-tuned models and 6 math reasoning benchmarks, and outperforms FLOP-matched beam search on 11/12 cells.

claims.claim: Single-configuration recursion is not reliably beneficial; gains come from aggregation over configurations.
claims.evidence_quote: A single L without aggregation sometimes degrades accuracy (e.g., Qwen2.5-3B / MATH-500 at L = 10: 61.6% vs. greedy 64.6%). The reliable gain comes from aggregating over the L-axis pool via EGLR-SC.

claims.claim: Training-free recursion must stay close to the anchor state: a small fusion weight is stable, large weights collapse because drift compounds.
claims.evidence_quote: drops sharply at α = 0.5 (56.6%, −8.4 pp), and collapses at α ≥ 0.7 (near-zero at 0.9). Large α erases the anchor signal; the recursion then compounds drift errors.

numbers.what: MATH-500 oracle accuracy, Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct: joint LxT vs T-only vs L-only
numbers.quote: on MATH-500 with Qwen2.53B-Instruct, the joint L×T oracle reaches 91.6%, +8.2 percentage points beyond the temperature-only oracle (83.4%)

numbers.what: EGLR-SC gain over greedy on MATH-500 across models
numbers.quote: On MATH-500, gains range from +1.8 pp (Qwen2.5-Math-7B) to +13.2 pp (Llama-3.1-8B), a universal, training-free lift from the L axis alone.

numbers.what: Kmax ablation on MATH-500 (Qwen2.5-3B, L=4)
numbers.quote: Accuracy rises from Kmax = 1 (63.2%) to Kmax = 3 (65.0%) then plateaus at Kmax = 4, 5 (64.8%, 64.6%).

numbers.what: Worst-case per-token overhead of a single EGLR run
numbers.value: below 5% over greedy (rho 0.05, Kmax 3, L 10, N 36)
numbers.quote: For ρ ≈ 0.05, Kmax = 3, L = 10, N = 36, worst-case overhead is below 5% over greedy.

numbers.what: Hyperparameters
numbers.quote: We use α = 0.2, Kmax = 3, τKL = 5×10−4 throughout.

numbers.what: Compute of FLOP-matched beam baseline
numbers.quote: Beam-11 is FLOP-matched to the full L = 0, . . . , 10 EGLR sweep (∼11.2× greedy).

limitations: Single L configurations show mixed gains (can degrade); KL early exit saturates at Kmax=3 and extending Kmax gives over-refinement; LxT pool analysis only on one model-dataset pair.
survey_notes: Training-free retrofit (sub-theme d). Loops the TOP-L layers (not middle layers), unlike 2605.23872 and ETD (2510.07358) which place the loop at mid-depth; a contrast for the 'which layers to loop' question. Stabilizes training-free recursion via anchor fusion (alpha<=0.2) and norm matching, analogous to the damped sub-stepping of 2605.23872: both find that the refined state must only nudge, not replace, the one-pass state. The headline gains rely on self-consistency over ~10 configurations (~11x compute); single-config recursion is near-neutral (65.0 vs 64.6 on MATH-500). Possible use as a rollout-diversity source for GRPO is proposed but not tested.

title: GramLoop: Training-Free Gram-Gated Replay for Robust Dense Prediction
relevance_reason: Training-free replay of a short block window in a frozen vision backbone (DINOv3), not a language model.
one_sentence: Replays blocks [21,23] of a frozen 40-block DINOv3 ViT-7B twice and gates each patchwise update by final-layer cosine-Gram drift from the standard trajectory, giving small robustness gains on shifted detection and segmentation benchmarks.
key_contributions: Training-free window replay in a frozen vision foundation model, controlled by a patchwise gate computed from final-layer Gram drift.
Separates where reliability is measured (final layer) from where the update is applied (loop endpoint); this placement is best in ablation.
At matched update strength, patchwise gating preserves Gram consistency better than uniform replay.

setup.model_sizes: DINOv3 ViT-7B/16 (40 blocks), frozen
setup.train_tokens_or_data: none (frozen backbone and heads)

title: Hopping Too Late: Exploring the Limitations of Large Language Models on Multi-Hop Queries
relevance_reason: Interpretability analysis; its back-patching (re-feeding a later-layer state into an earlier layer) is a one-off, oracle-selected training-free loop, motivating looping of pretrained layers.
one_sentence: Shows two-hop queries are resolved sequentially (bridge entity early, second hop late) so later layers may lack needed knowledge; patching a later-layer hidden state back into an earlier layer fixes up to 66% of failures with oracle layer choice.
key_contributions: Two-hop query dataset and Patchscopes-based localization of a sequential latent reasoning pathway.
Back-patching: re-running part of the forward pass from an earlier layer with a later-layer state, giving the model more layers without parameters or training.
Identifies that the second hop starts too late in depth, a mechanistic motivation for extra depth or looping.

Per-instance adjustment parameters (LoRA or parallel adapter) so each reuse of a shared tensor can specialize; without them gradient norms grow and fluctuate.
Ablations on reuse count (2 best, 3 worse), placement (interleave best for isotropic DeiT, stacking at tail for hierarchical Swin).

title: Retrofitting Recurrent Depth into a Pretrained Language Model: Installation, Extrapolation, Transfer, and Retention at Two Parameter Budgets
relevance_reason: Retrofits a pretrained dense LM (Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct) into a prelude/weight-tied recurrent block/coda model.
one_sentence: Converts Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct into a prelude/12-layer looped block/coda model with an identity-preserving gated re-entry bridge; per-loop intermediate-state supervision installs a stepwise operator (full-block 180M or 6M LoRA) that extrapolates about 1.5x its trained depth on a synthetic pointer-chasing task.

title: LoopUS: Recasting Pretrained LLMs into Looped Latent Refinement Models
relevance_reason: Post-training conversion of pretrained dense LLMs into encoder / looped reasoning block / decoder models.
one_sentence: Recasts Qwen3 (1.7B-8B), TinyLlama and Phi-4 into a shallow encoder, looped middle block and late decoder with a Mamba-style decay gate, random deep supervision with per-step detachment, a monotonicity loss and a confidence exit head, trained on 3B FineWeb-Edu tokens.
key_contributions: Block decomposition from layer-wise cosine-distance dynamics: tiny encoder (1-6 layers), 1 decoder layer, nearly the whole middle stack looped.
Input-dependent exponential-decay gate h' = a*M(h) + (1-a)*h as a damped, contraction-like update to limit hidden-state drift; SiLU monotonicity loss penalizes loops that raise next-token loss.
Random deep supervision: unroll B=20 loops, supervise K=5 uniformly sampled steps, detach between steps; reported to beat TBPTT in loss and cost.

Key design contrast: loops almost the entire stack (e.g. Qwen3-1.7B encoder 0-1, decoder 27) rather than a small middle block (ETD, McLeish), and uses no prelude re-injection, only a decay gate; contrasts with 2608.11233 and McLeish/Huginn which deem input injection necessary. title: Penelope: Localized Latent Recurrence for Efficient Structured Reasoning
relevance_reason: Retrofits a pretrained decoder (Llama-3.2-1B, Qwen3.5-0.8B) with weight-shared recurrence over a selected layer interval for latent reasoning.

title: LayerNorm as Implicit Gain Control in Looped Transformers
relevance_reason: Stability analysis of the recurrence in Parcae-style gated looped transformers (pre-LN block, constrained diagonal carry).
one_sentence: Shows analytically and at toy CPU scale that pre-LayerNorm inside a looped block couples its Lipschitz constant inversely to activation scale, making the recurrence Jacobian non-normal; the spectral margin, not operator norm, is the stability budget, and Parcae's carry constraint stabilizes rather than stores memory.

Identifies an activation-implosion failure mode (small activations -> Lipschitz spike -> divergence) and recommends monitoring per-token activation spread and max carry during training.

Shows gradient descent routes depth-memory through the nonlinear block rather than the constrained linear carry on cross-channel tasks; removing the carry constraint lets rho exceed 1 at high learning rate with state explosion hidden by the coda LayerNorm.

title: On the Residual Scaling of Looped Transformers: Stability and Transferability
relevance_reason: Derives residual-branch scaling and learning-rate transfer rules specific to weight-tied looped Transformers, tested in LM pretraining.

title: Stability and Generalization in Looped Transformers
relevance_reason: Fixed-point theory and small-scale experiments on which recurrence design choices (recall/input injection, outer normalization) give stable, extrapolating looped transformers.
one_sentence: Frames looped-network stability as reachability, input-dependence and geometry of fixed points; proves autonomous (no-recall) loops have countable fixed points, and shows recall plus outer normalization gives reachable, input-dependent fixed points that extrapolate better on chess, sudoku and prefix sums.

Shows recall (input injection) plus outer normalization yields fixed points that are reachable, smooth in the input, and independent of the initial iterate; introduces 'internal recall' placement.

title: Stabilizing Recurrent Dynamics for Test-Time Scalable Latent Reasoning in Looped Language Models
relevance_reason: Diagnoses divergence of looped LMs beyond the training loop horizon and adds a Jacobian spectral-radius regularizer to stabilize recurrence, tested on Ouro-1.4B.
one_sentence: Shows looped LMs (incl. Ouro-1.4B) peak at some loop depth then collapse; normalization placement trades stability against effectiveness, and STARS (Jacobian spectral-radius regularization via one-step JVP power iteration plus random loop sampling) curbs degradation beyond the training horizon.
key_contributions: Diagnosis on 4-digit addition with a single looped block: pre-norm (internal) lets hidden-state norm grow without bound and diverge past the training horizon; post-norm (external) stays bounded but settles in poor attractors; prelude/coda layers and L2 state-difference regularization do not fix this.
STARS: regularize squared Jacobian spectral radius (single-step power iteration with JVP) at a randomly sampled loop depth, combined with log-normal random loop sampling.

title: LoopMTP: A looped transformer guided by latent multi-token prediction
relevance_reason: From-scratch whole-stack looped LM with per-loop auxiliary (latent MTP) supervision and gated state aggregation.
one_sentence: LoopMTP loops a 12-layer 260M model, aligns loop t's hidden state (cosine) with the embedding of token t steps ahead, and aggregates all loop outputs with learned gates; it beats a parameter-matched non-looped model and LoopFormer at 6.8B tokens.
key_contributions: Latent soft multi-token prediction: per-loop cosine alignment of hidden state t to the (stop-gradient) output embedding of token i+t, a cheap per-loop auxiliary loss.
Gated softplus aggregation over all loop outputs (initialized to favor loop 1) plus a ponder KL-to-uniform regularizer, instead of overwriting the state.
Loop-LNS: fixed 1/T residual-branch scaling and per-iteration LayerNorms for stable training up to 15 loops without per-loop LR/WD/warmup tuning.

title: DeepLoop: Depth Scaling for Looped Transformers
relevance_reason: Residual-scaling/initialization rule for training stability of weight-tied looped transformers, with LM pretraining ablations.
one_sentence: DeepLoop shows weight tying makes shared updates aggregate across loop visits, derives a loop-aware DeepNorm rule (alpha=(2N)^1/2, beta=(8N)^-1/2), and improves looped GPT-2 small/medium validation loss at every R>=3 and HRM on ARC-AGI-1.

DeepLoop: Post-LN sandwich block with branch-input norm and alpha=(2N)^1/2, beta=(8N)^-1/2; no gates or auxiliary losses.

title: Scheduling Recursive Reasoning in Looped Transformers
relevance_reason: Adaptive per-loop update step size (relaxation) for looped/recurrent models (TRM, Ouro, Huginn, training-free looped Qwen3), plus a training-time trajectory regularizer.
one_sentence: TAPS replaces the unit recurrent update X_{k+1}=X_k+Delta with an online-adapted step size driven by a persistent-progress vs fluctuation decomposition; it raises terminal accuracy of frozen TRM, Ouro, Huginn and looped Qwen3, and a co-design regularizer adds gains on Sudoku/Maze.
key_contributions: Exact decomposition of the temporally averaged loss sensitivity to recurrent step size into persistent-progress and centered-fluctuation terms.
TAPS: training-free online step-size controllers (six estimators) that need no labels; sufficient conditions for reaching a target loss in fewer loops.
Training-inference co-design: penalty mu*sum ReLU(S_k - kappa P_k) added to the task+ACT loss during SFT of a TRM checkpoint.

title: Loop Dropout: Regularizing Shared Updates in Looped Language Models
relevance_reason: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning rule for pretrained looped LMs (Ouro, Huginn, LoopUS) that targets per-loop imbalance of a shared LoRA update.
one_sentence: Standard LoRA on looped LMs is late-loop biased; Loop Dropout masks whole adapter applications per loop with inverse-survival rescaling, improving GSM8K/MATH-500 fine-tuning of Ouro-1.4B/2.6B and depth extrapolation, at no inference cost.
key_contributions: Diagnostic: a LoRA adapter trained on Ouro-1.4B reduces loss 32% when applied only at loop 4 but 12% when applied only at loop 1 (late-loop bias).
Loop Dropout: Bernoulli masks over complete adapter applications at each loop (p=0.5) with division by survival probability; plain masking without rescaling does not help.
Gains over LoRA, LoRA+, CoTo, LoRA Dropout on Ouro; shared adapters with Loop Dropout beat per-loop independent adapters; larger gains when evaluated at more loops than trained.

title: Dense Supervision Is Not Enough: The Readout Blind Spot in Looped Language Models
relevance_reason: Controlled study of per-loop (dense) cross-entropy, readout normalization, and hidden-state norm drift in looped LMs.
one_sentence: Per-loop cross-entropy through scale-invariant (RMSNorm/LayerNorm) readouts trains usable early exits but cannot see hidden-state scale, so norms drift to tens of thousands in pre-norm loops; raw readouts, norm penalties, or inter-loop normalization fix it.
key_contributions: Readout blind spot: dense CE controls only the state variables the readout exposes; normalized readouts give ~zero radial gradient while pre-norm residual recurrence carries and updates scale.
2x2 ablation {terminal-only, per-loop CE} x {RMSNorm, raw readout} at 44M/129M plus norm-penalty and final-only-norm controls.

Norm drift makes models nearly K-invariant (extra loops barely change the normalized state), so its cost appears in the depth dimension; scale-controlled variants give a better PPL-throughput frontier.

setup.train_tokens_or_data: WikiText-103, 4 epochs, 3 seeds; 1.4B check on FineWeb ~1.3B tokens (50,000 steps)

claims.claim: Per-loop CE through RMSNorm readouts still lets final hidden-state norms drift into the tens of thousands in loops without inter-loop normalization; scale-visible readouts and norm penalties keep norms in the tens.

claims.evidence_quote: The resulting design rule is simple: dense supervision trains exits; recurrent scale control requires either making scale visible to a loss or removing it from the loop.

claims.claim: Norm drift costs depth use: RMSNorm per-loop models become nearly K-invariant (additional loops barely change the normalized state), whereas scale-controlled variants improve with more loops and achieve lower PPL at matched K/throughput.
claims.evidence_quote: with final-loop norms in the tens of thousands, angular updates shrink like 1/sk , so additional loops barely change the normalized state the readout sees.

numbers.quote: RMSNorm-readout drift is concentrated in a heavy tail of outlier tokens, especially under per-loop CE: the median is 12–21× smaller than the mean

limitations: Main evidence at 44M/129M on WikiText-103 with inter-loop normalization deliberately removed; architectures with inter-loop normalization, gating or clipping may avoid the failure; 1.4B check not a controlled ablation; teacher-forced scoring rather than autoregressive serving.
survey_notes: Links (b) stability and (c) deep supervision: per-loop CE (as in Ouro's exit-weighted per-loop loss) does not by itself prevent hidden-state norm growth; inter-loop normalization (Ouro, LoopMTP per-iteration LN) or a norm penalty does. Explains why some looped models become K-invariant (extra loops do nothing) despite dense supervision; relevant to 'depth extrapolation' claims. Complements Fully Looped Transformer 2605.18797 (residual explosion) and STARS 2605.26733 (Jacobian spectral radius). Small-scale; 1.4B check shows both variants K-invariant at 1.3B tokens, which also cautions that short-horizon Ouro-style training may not yet exploit loops.

title: What Makes Looped Transformers Perform Better Than Non-Recursive Ones
relevance_reason: Loss-landscape explanation of looped vs non-looped training dynamics plus a depth curriculum (train non-looped, then switch to looping).
one_sentence: Argues looping induces steep V-shaped valleys in a River-Valley loss landscape that let optimization keep progressing on complex patterns, and proposes SHIFT: train the single-pass model first, then switch to looping, matching looped accuracy with ~1.26x faster training on a toy task.
key_contributions: Empirical observations: looped attention shows a two-phase simple-to-complex learning curriculum and a three-phase Hessian eigenspectrum evolution (collapse, diversification, stabilization); single-pass and deeper non-looped (Deep-Attn) models stay static.

Extended River-Valley landscape theory distinguishing U-shaped (flat) and V-shaped (steep) valleys; theorems on deeper river exploration and positively aligned gradients between single-pass and looped models (shared river upstream).
SHIFT depth curriculum (T=1 then T>1) with a plateau-plus-patience switch criterion (SCP).

setup.loops_train: fixed loops in toy model; FOP-Loop-Adaptive (T loops for length-T sequences) on algorithmic tasks

setup.benchmarks: training/validation accuracy, length generalization accuracy, training time

claims.evidence_quote: We find that the spectral shape and evolution of Single-Attn (Figure 8) and Deep-Attn (Figure 10∼12) are nearly identical.

title: LoopRPT: Reinforcement Pre-Training for Looped Language Models
relevance_reason: RL objective applied directly to the latent loop steps and exit gate of Ouro looped LMs (1.4B, 2.6B).
one_sentence: Applies reinforcement pre-training to Ouro LoopLMs: entropy-selected hard tokens, per-loop rewards (log-prob gain vs EMA teacher minus time penalty), Gaussian-noise latent rollouts with GRPO on the exit step; small gains and fewer average loops.
key_contributions: Dense per-loop reward: student log-prob of the true next token at loop k minus EMA-teacher log-prob at the teacher's exit step, minus a difficulty-scaled time penalty.
On-policy exploration in latent space via Gaussian noise injected into recurrent hidden states; GRPO over sampled exit steps plus a step-weighted next-token representation loss.
Reduces average exit loops (e.g. 3.51 to 2.28 on hard tokens, Ouro-2.6B) with small benchmark gains over its own Ouro starting checkpoint.

survey_notes: Post-training (e): RL whose actions are latent loop/exit decisions, not tokens. Credit assignment: per-loop reward table R(k) = (student log-prob at loop k minus EMA-teacher log-prob at teacher exit step) minus time penalty; policy gradient over sampled exit steps from noise-perturbed recurrences (score-function, reward not backpropagated), plus a dense step-weighted per-loop NTP loss (deep supervision over loops; whether gradients are truncated across loops is not stated). title: Prioritize the Process, Not Just the Outcome: Rewarding Latent Thought Trajectories Improves Reasoning in Looped Language Models
relevance_reason: RLVR post-training of Ouro looped LMs, spreading the policy-gradient credit over every loop's next-token distribution.
one_sentence: Replaces GRPO's final-loop log-probability with a weighted sum of per-loop log-probabilities (exit-probability, progressive or uniform weights); on Ouro-1.4B/2.6B-Thinking it beats GRPO on math and transfers to non-math benchmarks.
key_contributions: RLTT: drop-in GRPO replacement whose policy gradient uses the weighted sum over loops of log P^(t)(y_j), so the outcome reward reaches every loop's readout.
Same-data, same-step, same-rollout comparison against GRPO on Ouro-1.4B/2.6B-Thinking, with paired significance tests and per-loop (1-4) evaluations.
Shows the only extra cost is memory, which grows linearly with loops (per-loop log-probs are kept); RLTT gives shorter responses and 10% less training time.

title: Latent Thinking Optimization: Your Latent Reasoning Language Model Secretly Encodes Reward Signals in Its Latent Thoughts
relevance_reason: Trains a reward model on Huginn-3.5B's per-recurrence latent states and uses it to select latent trajectories; the LM weights are not updated.
one_sentence: Shows Huginn-3.5B latent trajectories from correct and incorrect answers are separable, trains a small Latent Reward Model on them, and uses KL-regularized rejection sampling over random-init trajectories to beat majority voting at equal sample budget.
key_contributions: Analysis: Huginn-3.5B recurrent-step trajectories (T=32) that lead to correct answers are compact and convergent, while incorrect ones are dispersed; a classifier on the first few steps already predicts correctness.

Latent Reward Model (a 2-layer transformer encoder over the stacked latent states) plus LTO, an acceptance-rejection sampler for the KL-regularized optimal latent policy (best-of-N in the beta -> 0 limit).
Gains over majority voting and verbal or confidence self-correction at N=20 samples on math, commonsense and code; also applied to non-looped LLMs by treating layers as latent steps.

title: Energy-Entropy Regularization: The True Power of Minimal Looped Transformers
relevance_reason: Training regularizer for a tiny single-head looped transformer on a synthetic induction-head task; no language-model scale.
one_sentence: Adds Tsallis-entropy (attention contraction) and Hamiltonian kinetic/potential penalties to the loss so a d=8 single-head looped transformer learns induction heads and generalizes from training length 16-64 to length 1000.
key_contributions: Entropy-based contraction bound for single-head looped attention, motivating a Tsallis-entropy penalty that keeps the recurrence contractive.
Energy-entropy regularized objective (task + kinetic + potential + entropy terms) that reshapes the loss landscape to train a minimal looped model.
d=8 single-head looped model with T=25 loops reaches length-1000 induction accuracy beyond a larger FOP-Looped-Adaptive baseline.

title: Closing the Loop: Practical Training Recipes for Looped Language Models
relevance_reason: From-scratch and dense-to-loop training recipes for Ouro-style whole-stack looped LMs with controlled dense twins.
one_sentence: Two-stage 310B-token recipe for a 1.4B Ouro-architecture LoopLM (warmup plus larger exit-gate KL coefficient), a one-scalar dense-to-loop conversion of Qwen3-1.7B, and controlled dense twins matched in parameters, data, or inference compute.
key_contributions: From-scratch recipe: one 210B-token pretraining run plus 100B-token response-only mid-training at fixed T=4; LR warmup prevents early exit-gate collapse and beta=0.15 lets it recover; about 3% of Ouro's training compute.
Dense-to-loop conversion with one learned input-mixing scalar and an epsilon-smoothed exit loss; step-specific LoRA is optional.

Controlled comparisons: dense twins share data, stages and tokens, matched in parameters (1.4B) or in inference compute (3.9B); ablations of normalization placement, embedding injection, and RL (RLTT).

title: Teaching Pretrained Language Models to Think Deeper with Retrofitted Recurrence
relevance_reason: Converts pretrained fixed-depth LMs into Huginn-style prelude/recurrent-block/coda models via continued pretraining with a recurrence curriculum.
one_sentence: Performs model surgery on TinyLlama, OLMo-2 and Llama-3.2 1B models (drop middle layers, loop later layers with a concat adapter), trains with a curriculum over mean recurrence, and beats the parent model on math per training FLOP.
key_contributions: Pretrained-weight initialization of a (2,4,2) recurrent model beats random init per training FLOP; extrapolated loss curves cross only at roughly 950B tokens.
Curriculum that linearly or 1-sqrt schedules the mean of the Poisson-Lognormal recurrence distribution; scheduling max backprop depth is cheaper per FLOP but worse per step.
Recipe details: early layers as prelude, later layers as core and coda, Muon instead of AdamW, and a two-phase data curriculum with a FineWeb-Edu healing phase before high-quality data.

title: CHERRY: Compressed Hierarchical Experts with Recurrent Representational Yield
relevance_reason: Mostly a Korean sovereign-LM recipe paper; one component compresses a 48-layer model into a few weight-tied blocks unrolled recurrently (RDT).

Ordering matters: unrolling a freshly merged, untrained model raises loss sharply; healing first, then unrolling, lowers it.
Compressed looped configurations reach similar loss to each other across 227M-566M, but well above the uncompressed 48-layer original.

claims.claim: Normalization layers control the Lipschitzness of looped self-attention and keep the dynamics near criticality, which correlates with high accuracy.
claims.evidence_quote: It reveals that the normalization layer plays an essential role in suppressing the Lipschitzness of SA and the Jacobian’s complex eigenvalues, which correspond to the oscillatory components of the dynamics.

claims.claim: Energy-based regularization underperforms while Jacobian spectral regularization improves accuracy.
claims.evidence_quote: Energy-based regularization (“E-single” and “E-multi”) underperforms the original methods, while Jacobian spectral regularization (“Spec”) outperforms.

limitations: Small-scale Sudoku/CIFAR/LM settings; no large looped LMs.
venue: 39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2025).
survey_notes: (b) theory support for normalization between/inside loops and for spectral (Jacobian) regularization; agrees with 2605.26733 (STARS spectral-radius penalty) and 2607.10681 (spectral margin), and with 2604.15259 on normalization. Note it favors criticality (Lyapunov exponent near 0), not strict contraction.

title: Algorithmic Language Models with Neurally Compiled Libraries
relevance_reason: Adds an external differentiable interpreter with adaptive recurrence after LLaMA's last layer; the transformer layers themselves are not looped.
one_sentence: Augments LLaMA 3.2 with a neurally compiled differentiable computer (memory, registers, instructions, halting) and fine-tunes on simple variable-depth algorithmic tasks; feasibility study.
key_contributions: Differentiable library of compiled programs attached to an LLM, with adaptive recurrence in the interpreter.

setup.model_sizes: LLaMA 3.2 (1B) and minimal LLaMA-style models
setup.train_tokens_or_data: synthetic algorithmic tasks (Fibonacci, insertion sort, modular arithmetic)
setup.benchmarks: synthetic tasks

claims.claim: Recurrence lives in an attached differentiable interpreter rather than in looped transformer layers.
claims.evidence_quote: we add memory, registers, basic operations, and adaptive recurrence to a billion-parameter scale transformer architecture built on LLaMA3.2.

limitations: Feasibility study on simple synthetic tasks.
survey_notes: Out of scope for looped-in-depth training; exclude or cite only as tool-like recurrence.
